senses: void, null, invalid, without any legal use
la:adj:inutilis.html:
ĭn-ūtĭlis, e, adj.,
useless, unserviceable, unprofitable; constr. absol., with ad, or with dat. (class.).
In gen.
Of persons.
Absol.: homo iners atque inutilis,; ; : dum meliorem ex ducibus inutilem vulnus faceret,: turba,; .—Sup., .—
With ad: per aetatem ad pugnam inutiles,: ad rem gerendam,; .—
With dat.: aetate inutiles bello,: sibi,: reipublicae,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. things: rami,: naves ad navigandum inutiles,: tempestas non inutilis ad capiendum consilium,: impedimenta,: ferrum,: lingua,: alga,: et genus et nomen jactare,: inutiles oratori universales quaestiones,; : ad audiendum,.—With subj.-clause: quod non inutile sit imitari,; ; et saep.: stipulatio,invalid,: fidei commissa,.—Sup.: inutilissimus quisque,.—
Esp., hurtful, injurious.
Of persons: seditiosus et inutilis civis,; so : sed sibi inutilior,: mihi reique publicae,. —
Of inanim. and abstr. things: fungus,, n. 17: inutile est,; : aquae inutiles pestilentesque,: oratio,: arbitrium,.—Adv.: ĭnū-tĭlĭter.
Uselessly, unprofitably: non inutiliter,.—
Hurtfully, injuriously: late diffusa aqua bibitur inutilius,: administrare,.

la:verb:inuro.html:
ĭn-ūro, ussi, ustum, 3, v. a.,
to burn in, to burn.
Lit.: foramen,i. e. to make an uneven hole, such as is made by burning,.—Of encaustic painting: Nicias scripsit se inussisse,: cerae tinguntur isdem his coloribus ad eas picturas quae inuruntur,. — To burn in a mark: notas et nomina gentis,; : inustis barbarum litterarum notis,.—
To burn off or away, remove by burning: inustis infantum dexterioribus mammis ... unde Amazones dictae sunt,: ferro candente calcaribus inustis,; cf. .—
Trop., to brand, to imprint or attach indelibly: ne qua generi ac nomini suo nota nefariae turpitudinis inuratur,: quas ille leges fuit impositurus nobis atque inusturus?: aliquid calamistris, : censoriae severitatis nota inuri,: signa probitatis ... domesticis inusta notis veritatis,: acerbissimum alicui dolorem,: alicui famam superbiae et crudelitatis,: plurima mala rei publicae,: alicui ignominiam,: vivet semper in pectoribus illorum, quidquid istuc praesens necessitas inusserit,: nota turpitudinis inusta vitae alicujus,; : mihi dolorem,: ei dolorem,; cf.: hunc dolorem cineri ejus atque ossibus,. —Hence, ĭnustus, a, um, P. a., burned; subst.: inusta, ōrum, n., burned parts, burns, .

la:adj:inultus.html:
ĭn-ultus, a, um, adj.
For whom no revenge is taken, unavenged, unrevenged, not vindicated.
Of persons: Marius ne inultus esset,: ne inultos imperatores suos jacere sinerent,: moriemur inultae?: non me inulto Victor laetabere,; ; : quam inulti perierint,; Dietsch; .—
Of things: mortem suam ne inultam pateretur,: injuriae,: cruor,: nil poterit Juno, nisi inultos flere dolores?: nec Ptolemaeo inulta scelera fuerunt,: Alexandro caedes,.—
Upon whom no revenge is taken, unpunished.
Of persons: numquam me inultus istic ludificabit,: cur Asellium esse inultum tam diu sinis,: hostīs inultos abire sinere,; : hostis Medeae nullus inultus,. —
Transf.
Of things, for which no punishment is inflicted, unpunished: neque scelus inultum relinquendum,; : quicquid multis peccatur, inultum est,.—
Unharmed, unhurt, safe, with impunity: inulto Dicere quod sentit permitto,: neu sinas Medos equitare inultos,; cf.: at ne illud haud inultum, si vivo, ferent ( = inulti),: sed inultum numquam id auferet,: et catulos ferae Celent inultae,.—
Trop., unsated, unappeased, insatiable: odium,; cf. preces,unavailing,.

la:verb:inundo.html:
ĭn-undo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
Act., to overflow, inundate (class.).
Lit.: terram inundet aqua,: imbres campis inundantes,: Tiberis agros inundavit,; ; : Ciliciam cruore Persarum,: cruore campos,.—
Transf., to spread over, run over, flood: inundant Troes,: Cimbros inundasse Italiam,: multitudo inundaverat campos,: Europam,: totam urbem civilis sanguinis fluminibus,: armis campos,.—
Trop.: lacrimae pectus,: meus ingenti flumine litterarum inundata,overflowing,; .—
Neutr.
To overflow, to be inundated or deluged; of a river: Arnus inundaverat,: Tiberis,: aquae super terram,; .—
To be full, abound: inundant sanguine fossae,; .
la:verb:inundo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:inumbro.gloss: to cast a shadow upon, shade, darken
senses: to cast a shadow upon, shade, darken
la:verb:inumbro.html:
ĭn-umbro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to cast a shadow upon, to shade (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn. opaco).
Lit.: terraque inumbratur,: toros obtentu frondis,: forum velis,; ; .—
Transf.
To cause darkness: inumbrante vespera,.—
To cover: ora coronis,: pubem pallio,: ante genas quam flos juvenilis inumbret, Claud. Prob. et Olyb. 69.—
To mark the shadows upon, to mark out, lay out (anteclass.): solarium, Müll. —
Trop., to obscure: imperatoris adventu legatorum dignitas inumbratur,: inumbrata quies,apparent,.

la:verb:inunguo.html:
ĭn-unguo (not -go), unxi, unctum, 3, v. a.,
to anoint (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: oculos,: non tamen idcirco contemnas lippus inungui,; ; : inunguendum primo lenibus,.—
In gen., to besmear: lentem siccatam oleo,; : conchis inuncta,dressed with oil,.

la:adj:inusitatus.html:
ĭn-ūsĭtātus, a, um, adj.,
unusual, uncommon, extraordinary, very rare (class.): pro di immortales! speciem humanam inusitatam, Att. ap. : nova et inusitata belli ratio,: magnitudo,: lepor,.— With dat.: nostris oratoribus lepos,; : inusitatum est, with subj.-clause, . — Comp.: species navium inusitatior,.—Sup.: miracula, , 10, 12.—Adv. in two forms.
ĭnūsĭ-tātē, in an unwonted manner, unusually, strangely: absurde et inusitate scriptae epistolae,: loqui,.—Comp.: poëta inusitatius contraxerat,.—Sup.: inusitatissime nox pro noctu dixerunt (al. inusitate),.—*
ĭnūsĭtātō, in an unusual manner: enituit, (al. inusitato indicio enituit).

la:noun:inundatio.html:
ĭnundātĭo, ōnis, f.
inundo
,
an overflowing, inundating, inundation (postAug.): fluminum,: coërcere,: inundationes Tiberis,: Nili,; : terrarum,the deluge,; . —
Transf., of a crowd of people, Schol. .— Of horses: inundatione equorum ejus operiet te pulvis,.—Of troubles, sorrow, .

la:adj:inurbanus.html:
ĭn-urbānus, a, um, adj.,
rustic, boorish, rude, unpolishcd, unmannerly (class.): habitus orationis non inurbanus,: non essem tam inurbanus ac paene inhumanus,: gestus,: inurbanum lepido seponere dicto,.—Adv.: inurbānē, rudely, inelegantly, without wit or humor: non inurbane,; ; and, inurbānĭter (late Lat.), Aug. c. Faust. Manich. 12, 1.
